title: Consolidated security request intake, automated risk-scoring, and routing playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit security and compliance requirements (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR, DPAs, vendor questionnaires) through email, sales notes, support tickets and ad-hoc RFP attachments. The current process is ad-hoc: requests land in multiple inboxes, instrumentation is poor, priority decisions are manual, and triage time-to-first-response varies widely. This causes missed SLAs, duplicated work between Security/Legal/Support, and opaque status for account teams.

Goal: Design a single, lightweight intake form + backend scoring model that consolidates security asks, classifies them by compliance domain and risk, and routes them to the correct resolver (security engineer, legal, solutions engineering, or self-serve content). Produce an operational playbook that defines SLAs, routing rules, escalation paths, and reporting requirements. The solution should reduce time-to-triage, provide repeatable prioritization, and enable measurable SLAs for enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: A single hosted intake form exists and is linked from Sales playbooks, Support KB, and the enterprise onboarding checklist
Backend risk-scoring prototype returns a stable classification (compliance domain + high/medium/low risk) for >90% of sample requests in pilot set
Routing rules route 95% of pilot requests to the correct resolver queue without manual override
Dashboard shows intake volume, average time-to-triage, SLA compliance, and top request categories
Playbook with clear SLAs and escalation paths is published and signed off by Security, Legal, and Sales
recent_updates: 2025-02-12: Discovery interviews completed with 6 enterprise customers and GTM (sales + AM) — common asks: DPA, data residency, encryption, SOC2 evidence bundles
2025-02-18: Workshop with Security & Legal to map resolution owners for common request types; agreed to 3-tier routing: self-serve, security-led, legal-led
2025-02-22: Prototype intake form v0 created in Google Forms + spreadsheet scoring; initial scoring rules based on data sensitivity and contract exposure
2025-02-26: Engineering scoped API endpoint and queue integration; ENG estimate for POC backend service: 3 points (ENG-8420)
2025-02-28: Pilot agreement signed with two customers to route non-sensitive questionnaire items through the intake form for 4-week pilot
proposed_solution: Implement a consolidated web intake that captures structured metadata (customer, environment, data types, contract clauses requested, requested SLAs, required artifact types). Run a rule-based + feature-weighted risk scorer (factors: data sensitivity, PII/PHI, regulatory domain, contract exposure, legal clause count, requester role) to assign a risk level and primary resolver. Store intake records in a centralized queue with tags for resolution path. Integrate with Console (ticket links and dashboard) so account teams can see status. Publish the playbook that enumerates routing rules, committed triage SLAs (initial triage within 48 hours for high risk, 5 business days for medium), and escalation owners. Pilot for 30 days, iterate scoring weights based on observed classification accuracy and resolver feedback.
tradeoffs: Rule-based scorer is faster to implement but will require manual tuning and edge-case handling; an ML model is more flexible but increases complexity and data needs
Aggressive automation reduces manual load but risks misrouting sensitive items — mitigated by a manual override and audit trail
Tighter SLAs require additional headcount or queue automation for scale; initial implementation focuses on automation and self-serve to limit headcount spend
blocking_items: Security sign-off on automated routing for PHI-containing requests
Legal approval of the public intake form language and data handling disclosures
Engineering capacity to add intake API + queue integration (dependency ENG-8420)
next_steps: Week 1: Finalize intake form fields and canonical taxonomy with Security/Legal/GTM
Week 2: Build backend risk-scoring prototype and queue integration (ENG kickoff ticket ENG-8420)
Week 3: Launch closed pilot with two enterprise customers; instrument dashboards
Week 4: Collect pilot feedback, adjust scoring weights and routing rules
Post-pilot: Publish playbook, open rollout to all enterprise customers, add retention reporting to Console
